question: Who among the following was re-elected in 1938 as the president of the Indian National Congress session for 1939?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhash Chandra Bose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• He was elected as the President of the Indian National Congress in 1938 and was re-elected in 1939.
 
• Bose's leadership was characterized by his strong stance on complete and immediate independence for India, as opposed to the gradual approach advocated by other leaders.
 
• His re-election in 1939 led to significant internal conflicts within the Congress, eventually leading to his resignation from the presidency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• The INC was founded in 1885 and played a major role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• It was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement, with over 15 million members and over 70 million participants.
 
• The INC's influence waned after India gained independence in 1947, but it remains one of the two major political parties in India.
 
 
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose**
 
 
• Bose was an Indian nationalist whose defiant patriotism made him a hero in India, but his legacy remains controversial due to his collaboration with Axis powers during World War II.
 
• He believed that the Gandhian non-violence approach was not sufficient to secure India’s independence and advocated for armed struggle.
 
• In 1943, he formed the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) with the help of Japan to fight against British rule.
 
• His famous slogan was "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!"
 
 
 
• **Internal Conflict within the INC**
 
 
• Bose's re-election as INC president in 1939 was opposed by Mahatma Gandhi and his supporters.
 
• Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by Bose, causing a rift within the party.
 
• The ideological differences between Bose and the Gandhian faction led to Bose's resignation and the formation of the Forward Bloc within the Congress.
